newsitem.title: UK: Profit-taking to curb any Italian bond ERM gains.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking to curb any Italian bond ERM gains.

text.p: Italian bonds will get a boost if Italy's plans to reenter the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) go ahead, but investors may use the chance to lock in profits from a year of spectacular gains, analysts said on Friday.
"There is a risk people will start to take profits," said Adrian Owens, senior economist at Julius Baer in London.

Longer-term, the debate is open as to whether positive economic fundamentals will allow the market to continue to surge or whether a reassessment of Italy's single European currency credentials will cause investors to flee, they said.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Friday the Italian government had asked for the lira to reenter the ERM, a currency grid that sets fluctuation limits for member units.

Markets were already on the move before the news amid talk the lira would reenter the ERM this weekend, boosting BTP futures on LIFFE and sending cash yields lower against other European debt markets.
By 1457 GMT, December BTP futures on LIFFE were quoted at 128.14, up 87 basis points on the day and the 10-year BTP/Bund cash yield spread was at 172 compared with 179 late on Thursday.
The BTP/Bund gap started 1996 at around 475 basis points.
Italian bonds have surged all year on the belief that the lira would rejoin the ERM and that it may even be in the first Round of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
But analysts said many investors would use the opportunity to rack up their gains, and the spread was likely to contract another 10 basis points or so before pushing out again.

"I would have thought assuming they go in the weekend, you'll have a quick trade to 160 over and then, there will be an enormous amount of profit-taking," Mark Fox, chief European strategist in fixed income at Lehman Brothers in London.
